title: Supplier Evaluation Evidence Kit & DPA Clause Bank
body:
Purpose:
This working-kit is intended as a practical, operational artifact for security, legal, and procurement teams to accelerate evidence collection for vendor security assessments and to provide ready-to-use DPA clause language for common negotiation points. Treat as a living document: copy into vendor-specific intake folders and edit the checklist per risk profile.

Scope and intended users:
- Security & Compliance: primary consumer for evidence requests and risk triage.
- Legal / Procurement: use clause bank when drafting or negotiating DPAs and SLAs.
- Solutions/SEs and Customer-Facing teams: surface ask lists early in RFPs

How to use this kit (quick workflow):
1) Determine risk band: low / medium / high (see decision matrix below).
2) Pick the evidence bundle for that band.
3) Share bundle with vendor via intake form and set a 2-week follow-up cadence for high-risk vendors.
4) Legal picks relevant DPA clauses from clause bank and proposes as redlines.
5) Security reviews submitted evidence, documents gaps and mitigation plan.

Decision matrix (high level):
- Low: SaaS tools processing no customer data or only anonymized telemetry. Evidence: SOC2 report or equivalent, minimal questionnaire.
- Medium: Tools that process low sensitivity PII or limited customer data; require DPA with standard assurances, documented encryption, and access controls.
- High: Vendors processing regulated data, customer content, or with hosting in non-standard geographies — require full evidence set, encryption key management controls, penetration test results, and on-site audit rights.

Evidence checklist (copy into intake):
Core (all vendors):
- Latest SOC 2 Type II (or equivalent) report (PDF) and scope page
- Attestation letter or executive summary of controls
- Security contact and escalation path (name, email, phone)
- High-level network/infra diagram (redacted as needed)
- Vulnerability management policy summary (scan cadence)
- Data classification and handling summary

Additional (medium):
- Results of recent external pentest (last 12 months) or remediation plan
- Role-based access control description and sample IAM policy
- Encryption in transit (TLS version) and encryption at rest details (algorithms, KMS used)
- Subprocessor list and subprocessors' SOC-type summary
- Retention & deletion flow (how data is purged when requested)

Required (high):
- Penetration test report with remediation evidence (or contractually committed remediation timeline)
- KMS architecture and key rotation procedure (if vendor manages keys)
- Data location confirmation and cross-border transfer mechanisms (standard contractual clauses, SCCs, or adequacy)
- Incident response runbook and recent tabletop summary
- Right-to-audit annex and sample audit scope

Red flags to escalate to legal/security: (do not wait)
- Vendor refuses to provide any third-party attestation (SOC2 / ISO27001)
- No documented encryption or vague answers about key management
- Subprocessor list is blank or changes frequently without notice
- Vendor cannot commit to deletion/return of data within a reasonable SLA
- No formal incident response process or no evidence of past incident handling

Practical intake language (short, copy-paste into outreach):
Hi <VENDOR_CONTACT>,

As part of our standard vendor intake, please provide the following artifacts within 10 business days: SOC2 Type II (or equivalent) report, data handling summary, network diagram, and answers to the attached questionnaire (see Appendix A). If any artifact is unavailable, please flag and provide a remediation/mitigation timeline.

Clause bank — suggested DPA language snippets (operational, not legalese-heavy; adapt to jurisdiction & legal review):
1) Purpose limitation (simple):
"Vendor shall process Customer Personal Data only to perform the services set forth in the Agreement and in accordance with Customer's documented instructions. Vendor will not use Customer Personal Data for profiling, marketing, or other purposes not directed by Customer."

2) Data locality & transfers:
"Vendor shall store and process Customer Personal Data only in the regions specified in Schedule X. Any transfer of Personal Data outside these regions must be subject to appropriate safeguards, including [SCCs/standard contractual clauses] or other lawful mechanism, and Vendor must notify Customer at least 30 days prior to the transfer."

3) Encryption & keys (vendor-managed keys):
"Vendor shall encrypt Customer Personal Data at rest using industry standard algorithms (e.g., AES-256) and in transit using TLS 1.2+ (or equivalent). For vendor-managed keys, Vendor will document key generation, rotation, destruction procedures and provide Customer with key custody options where feasible."

4) Customer-managed keys (optional stronger control):
"Where Customer elects to manage cryptographic keys, Vendor shall support Customer's KMS integration and shall not have the ability to access plaintext Customer Personal Data without Customer's explicit authorization."

5) Subprocessor / subcontractor flow:
"Vendor may engage subprocessors only with Customer's prior written consent. Vendor shall maintain an up-to-date list of subprocessors, provide notice of changes at least 30 days prior to onboarding, and flow down equivalent data protection obligations in written contracts."

6) Data deletion & return:
"Upon expiration or termination of the Agreement, Vendor shall, at Customer's election, return or securely delete all Customer Personal Data within [30] days, certify deletion, and provide evidence of secure erasure for any backups within a commercially reasonable window."

7) Incident notification & cooperation:
"Vendor shall notify Customer without undue delay, and in any event no later than 72 hours, after becoming aware of a confirmed security breach affecting Customer Personal Data. Vendor shall provide a root cause analysis, scope of affected data, remedial steps taken, and a remediation timeline."

8) Audit rights & on-site assessments:
"Customer shall have the right, upon reasonable notice and during normal business hours, to conduct audits or inspections (including on-site) to verify Vendor's compliance with security obligations. Vendor shall cooperate and provide reasonable access to evidence and personnel."

Negotiation playbook — tips for triage between Legal and Security:
- If vendor provides strong third-party attestations (SOC2 + external pentest) and the risk band is low/medium, default to standard DPA with clauses 1–6.
- For high risk or regulated data, require customer-managed keys OR extra contractual protections (SCCs + audit rights + retention commitments).
- Always demand a subprocessors list and notice period — that is low cost to vendor and high signal for us.

Appendix A — Short vendor questionnaire (copy into intake form):
1) Do you maintain any independent security attestation (SOC2 Type II / ISO27001)? If yes, attach the latest report and state the scope and date.
2) Do you use third-party subprocessors to process customer data? Provide an up-to-date list and locations.
3) What encryption is used in transit and at rest? Provide algorithms and key management details.
4) Do you offer customer-managed keys (BYOK/HSM)? If yes, describe integration steps.
5) What is your incident response SLA for customer notification? Provide last incident summary and remediation.
6) Data retention default and deletion process (how long, how removed on request)?
7) Is any customer data processed/stored outside of the vendor's home jurisdiction? If yes, list countries and cross-border mechanisms.
8) Do you permit on-site audits? If not, provide explanation and alternative evidence.

Evidence submission checklist (compact, for vendor UI):
- [ ] SOC2 Type II (or ISO27001 cert)
- [ ] Pen test report (redacted OK) or remediation plan
- [ ] Data handling summary + retention policy
- [ ] Network/infra diagram (redacted)
- [ ] Subprocessor list with locations

Common negotiation shortcuts (practical):
- If vendor will not accept full audit rights, ask for a tailored 'desk audit' package: scoped evidence, named POA for 30 days.
- For encryption gaps, require a documented roadmap with contractual milestone credits or termination right if not delivered.
- For subprocessors with limited visibility, require quarterly attestation and breach notification obligations to be contractually reinforced.

Open questions / TODOs (working notes):
- Decide default retention period to propose for SaaS telemetry (30/90/365 days) — security prefers 90 days, product prefers 365 for analytics.
- Confirm approved wording for BYOK options (legal to finalize in next draft).
- Create quick intake form template in Google Forms and wire to vendor-onboarding Slack channel. (Action: Ellen Park)

Revision history:
- 2024-11-10: Initial draft by Aisha Patel
- 2024-11-20: Added negotiation playbook and clause snippets (Ravi Srinivasan)
- 2024-12-03: Added intake language and updated evidence checklist (Luis Romero)

Notes to reviewers:
This is intentionally operational rather than exhaustive legal language. Legal should convert suggested snippets into fully qualified clauses with jurisdictional references. Security should keep the evidence checklist synced to our internal controls matrix. Procurement: feel free to add cost-specific negotiation playbooks (credits, SLA credits, termination triggers).
